Character Description: Ramona is sixteen. A deeply intelligent and layered young woman, Ramona also doesn't feel defined at all by growing up without a mother. She is independent. Outwardly confident. Has a genius sense of humor. She has a heaviness that a lot of young people try to put on to feel mature but Ramona's actually trying to hide it because it's dark. So dark she's afraid it will scare people away. Ramona was raised by her grandfather in a blue collar town and learned early how to take care of herself, how to read a room, and how to disappear when she needs to. Underneath the wit is a fierce loyalty to the few people she lets in, and a quiet hope that someone will finally see all of her and not look away.
Late 40s, weathered and sardonic. A career detective who has seen too much and trusts too little, but still shows up every day because the work is the only thing that makes sense.
